hypotheses.title: Connection-pool exhaustion triggered by an unindexed facet aggregation from feature flag faceted_search_v2
hypotheses.summary: At 14:02 the faceted_search_v2 flag was enabled and added an unindexed brand.keyword aggregation to every search query, holding each database connection ~8x longer. The fixed 20-connection pool saturated (active=20, waiting=180) and search returned 503s until the flag was disabled at 14:41 and the pool drained. Pool exhaustion is the failure mechanism; the flag-driven facet query is the trigger.
unknowns: The configured pool maximum is inferred from active=20/20; the actual pool sizing is not in evidence.
No per-query connection-hold-time metric is captured to directly confirm the ~8x figure.
validation_steps: Confirm the pool max is 20 and correlate connection-hold time before and after 14:02.
Reproduce a faceted query in staging and measure connections held versus the non-faceted path.

remediation_items.description: Add an index (eager_global_ordinals) for the brand.keyword facet so the aggregation stops full-scanning and releases connections quickly.
Gate feature flags that change the query path behind a load test and enforce the staged 5%/25% rollout the guardrail skipped.
Right-size and bulkhead the connection pool with a short acquisition timeout so a slow query path degrades instead of exhausting the pool.

hypotheses.title: A no-backoff client retry storm amplified the pool exhaustion
hypotheses.summary: As latency rose, clients retried without backoff: retry rate climbed to 3.1x baseline and duplicate query signatures appeared, tripling effective load on the already-saturated pool. This is an amplifying condition, not the initiating cause.
unknowns: Whether retries came from first-party clients, the SDK default, or an upstream gateway.
validation_steps: Attribute the 3.1x retry rate to a client/SDK and confirm it lacked exponential backoff.

remediation_items.description: Add exponential backoff with jitter and a circuit breaker so retries shed load instead of compounding it.

hypotheses.title: Flash-sale traffic surge amplified but did not by itself cause the outage
hypotheses.summary: Flash-sale traffic ran at ~3x baseline (2550 rps) and raised concurrency on the pool. But a higher-traffic sale the prior week (3200 rps) ran with zero errors, so the surge is an amplifying condition that made the triggered mechanism worse, not a standalone cause.
unknowns: Whether the prior sale ran with the same pool size and query path for a clean comparison.
validation_steps: Compare the 05-07 sale's pool utilization and query path against 05-14 to isolate the flag's contribution.

hypotheses.title: The v4.7.1 deploy regressed search (rejected)
hypotheses.summary: The 14:00 deploy is the obvious suspect but is not supported: it shipped the faceted_search_v2 code with the flag OFF, the flag was flipped on 2 minutes later by a separate automated job, and a rollback did not stop the 503s.
unknowns: Whether any non-flagged code in v4.7.1 touched the search path at all.
validation_steps: Diff v4.7.1 for any unflagged change to the search query or pool configuration.

hypotheses.title: An Elasticsearch cluster or hardware fault (rejected)
hypotheses.summary: A datastore fault would explain slow queries, but the cluster stayed green with normal CPU and heap and no restarts or shard moves throughout, so a cluster/hardware fault is unsupported.
unknowns: Whether a single hot shard could degrade without moving the cluster off green.
validation_steps: Check per-shard latency for a hot shard that a green cluster status could mask.
